label: Kyriba claim boundary
query: If Kyriba is not live yet, what exactly can Lakeshore claim today without overstating value?
answer: You can credibly claim Kyriba as a well‑advanced, high‑intent initiative, but not as an in‑production source of realized business value yet. Grounded in your current spine for LSH-KYRIBA-TREASURY-2026: 1) What you can safely claim today – Strategy and design maturity: Business case, strategy, and solution design are approved through BAFO. You can say: • “Lakeshore has completed vendor selection and BAFO with Kyriba for enterprise treasury management.” • “Target-state cash, liquidity, and bank-connectivity model is defined, with board/CFO-aligned value hypotheses (e.g., improved cash visibility, reduced idle balances, tighter controls).” – Program posture: • “Kyriba is our selected treasury platform, currently in pre–executive decision / pre-contract finalization, with implementation planning underway.” – Risk/governance: • “We’ve run Kyriba through structured evaluation, including architecture, security, and integration fit (with Mulesoft/low‑criticality integration patterns already mapped at high level).” 2) What you should not claim yet Given Executive Decision, Selection (final), Transition, and Value are still review/needs‑review: – No live status: Don’t say “Kyriba is implemented,” “in production,” “live in treasury,” or imply any cutover from legacy banking/treasury tools. – No realized value: Avoid concrete outcome language like “we have reduced idle cash by X%,” “automated Y% of payments,” or “improved liquidity forecasting accuracy” tied to Kyriba. Any numbers must be framed as targets, not achieved. – No final contractual posture: Don’t imply a fully executed MSA/SOW stack or locked‑in term/price unless and until Executive Decision is marked complete in the spine.Evidence checked: intake.tenant_context (loaded tenant context), telemetry.value_attestation (verified versus projected value), intake.missing_fields (missing or stale evidence fields), intake.question_scope (question scope).
